summary.text: Suzie Byrd, a Democratic former reporter for the Enid News, lost the November 3, 2026 election for Oklahoma's 3rd District to Frank Lucas.

According to her Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey, she grew up in Oklahoma, was a college athlete at Oklahoma State University, has owned or partnered in more than a dozen businesses, and worked nearly four years as a reporter for the Enid News before resigning to run for Congress.

paragraphs.text: Suzie Byrd describes herself as born and raised in Oklahoma, with grandparents who farmed in southwest Oklahoma and a father who worked in the oil field.
She graduated from Hennessey High School, where she says she was an All-State athlete in basketball and track.

She earned a bachelor's degree from Oklahoma State University in 1976 and says her degree is in journalism; she says she played basketball for one year and ran track for two, was a two-time Big 8 champion, and was the school's first female All-American.
Byrd says she has owned or been a partner in more than 12 businesses in Oklahoma and Florida.
She says she was a reporter for the Enid News for almost four years, writing about education, healthcare, abuse and contamination of farmland, before resigning to run for Congress.
She says she has two daughters and two grandchildren, lives in Enid, and built her own barn house out of an interest in affordable housing.
She said her campaign focused on universal healthcare, affordable housing and a livable wage, and a fairer tax code.
She received 36.0% of the vote to Frank Lucas's 64.0%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
